title: Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes and No-FOMO Action Plan
web_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
question: What must be true for TANFAC’s growth plan to compound—and what do you do with new cash and the current holding?

epigraph.quote: The Company’s ability to commission the project within the estimated cost and timeline, stabilise the operations and achieve a timely ramp-up in sales will remain the key monitorables.
epigraph.author: ICRA, October 16, 2026 [7]

web_blocks.text: The strongest bull case is operationally specific. TANFAC has captive sulphuric acid, in-house HF, high FY26 utilization in its established core and a qualified solar-grade DHF product whose capacity has been debottlenecked to 25,000 TPA. The HFC-32 project was about 90% complete by the November 3 call, part of the planned output was under long-term supply arrangements, and management expects 95% utilization in FY28. If commissioning is on time, buyers qualify supply, 55–60% FY28 revenue growth arrives and the 24–26% EBITDA-margin guide is approached, revenue mix and operating leverage could improve materially. [1][2][4][6]

The steelman bear case is not that fluorine chemistry lacks demand. It is that TANFAC’s economics still depend on volatile HF and sulphur spreads, imported fluorspar, a single Cuddalore site, working capital and timely utilization of new assets. FY25/FY26 free cash flow was negative after investment; FY26 CFO ₹43.4 crore was below PAT ₹70.1 crore; H1 FY27 margins and PAT softened even as sales grew. The new plant and ₹250-crore future AHF/solar capex consume capital before their full cash returns are visible. ICRA cites Chinese/import competition, end-market cyclicality, policy/transport risks and execution as rating monitorables. [1][4][6][7]

web_blocks.text: The hinge claim is not the size of the market; it is the cash yield on the capital required to serve it. The forward guidance compounds from a FY26 base, and the company’s next phase also includes further capex and a temporarily higher raw-material inventory position. A reasonable analyst can be wrong in either direction: the low FCF assumptions may understate the post-commissioning cash surge, or the growth guide may overstate the share of capacity that becomes qualified, shipped and collected. That is why the base case uses a modest exit multiple and the bull case remains a separate tail, not the default. [1][4][6][7]

web_blocks.text: Adversarial margin stress: change one assumption from the base case—FY28 EBITDA margin falls from 25% to 20%—and keep revenue ₹1,539.92 crore, D&A ₹35 crore, finance ₹8 crore, other income ₹4 crore, tax 25%, shares 2.181 crore and exit multiple 23.5x. EBITDA becomes ₹307.98 crore; PAT becomes ₹201.74 crore; EPS becomes ₹92.49; value is ₹2,174 per share. That is a 35.1% downside from CMP. This is an analyst stress assumption, not a company forecast; it reinforces the exit decision unless later filings show the margin and cash path improving. [1][4][6][12]

web_blocks.text: The verdict for new capital is REJECTED, not because the company has failed, but because the current evidence does not make the support band investable. The technical reference area is ₹2,933–₹3,031; the base value is ₹2,800, so the base reward is negative at the top of the zone and the anti-hedging hurdle fails. The ₹2,850 level is a chart invalidation reference for a future setup; it is not a reason to hold a position whose expected value is below CMP. If the stock revisits support, repeat the DCF and EPS bridge with new filings; do not treat a lower price as sufficient by itself. [1][6][12][35] The same valuation logic applies to the existing holding: the expected-value case is negative at CMP, so the recommendation is to exit the current 55-share position rather than wait for the structural stop. book_paragraphs: Before we write the action, let us give the bull case its full voice. TANFAC has not simply announced a plant; it built an integrated base, expanded HF, commissioned two phases of solar-grade DHF, won customer qualification and raised equity for downstream investment. The Q2 call says the new HFC-32 facility was around 90% complete by September, with planned commissioning in Q3 FY27. Part of capacity is covered by long-term arrangements, and management speaks to high FY28 utilization. If the plant starts safely, buyers accept the product, and volume flows through the captive HF chain, the operating leverage can be real. [1][2][4][6]

Now let the bear answer. HFC-32 has not yet generated a full commercial year of sales. The ₹250-crore next-phase capex competes for cash with working capital and further expansion. FY26 operating cash flow was ₹43.4 crore against ₹70.1 crore PAT, and capital spending was ₹82.4 crore. H1 FY27 margins declined even as revenue rose, with management attributing part of the move to realizations, raw-material costs, freight and low early-stage margins on new products. The company’s explanation may prove right; a skeptical analyst still waits for the reversal to appear in cash, not only in commentary. [1][4][5][6]

A scenario table forces us to own both sides. Our bear case is ₹1,300 if commissioning, spreads or utilization disappoint and the multiple contracts. Our base is ₹2,800, based on management’s growth and margin guidance but a 23.5-times exit multiple for cash and scale risk. Our bull is ₹5,000 if HFC-32, solar-grade DHF and future products all scale with durable margins. Assigning 30%, 50% and 20% gives a weighted ₹2,790, below the ₹3,349.40 price. You may change the probabilities, but you should not hide them behind “long-term story.” [1][6][12]

What does that mean for the existing holder? The same-session ledger reports 55 shares, ₹184,217 market value, a ₹173,945.55 cost basis and a 4.28% portfolio weight. This is a moderate position, not a portfolio emergency. The weighted value is below CMP, so we recommend exiting all 55 shares at the next available session after checking the live quote. The company is not a fundamental failure, but the price and cash-conversion risk do not justify retaining the current position. No broker order is placed. The alert is an instruction for review, not an electronic order. [35]

Redeployment is where discipline becomes visible. We compare TANFACIND in the active shortlist, Alufluoride as the closest product-screen outside name, and larger fluorochemical peers. The shortlist candidate’s base value is below its support reference. Alufluoride’s snapshot valuation and ROCE look more modest, but it has only 60 daily bars and lacks a full underwriting; the simple multiple reference produces less than one-to-one reward against the chosen stop. Navin, Gujarat Fluorochemicals and SRF are useful peer contexts, not pre-approved substitutes. So the next marginal cash unit stays 100% cash. We will fund an equity only when business quality, live price, support and cash evidence align. [12][34][35]

The sale proceeds are not yet cash; the report makes no transaction. If the 55-share exit is executed near the November 13 close, about ₹184,217 before costs and slippage becomes the capital pool. Keep that pool in cash. The bull case remains possible, but the scenario bridge assigns it only 20% because commissioning, qualification, margins and cash have not yet been shown together. The price may recover; the point is not to predict the next tick, but to stop a weak expected-value position from consuming fresh attention and risk budget. [4][6][7]

What would make you and me revise this conclusion? First, evidence that the HFC-32 plant commissioned on schedule and delivered repeat qualified shipments, not only trial output. Second, margins that approach management’s stated range without relying on an unusually favorable input spread. Third, cash conversion that improves after the bulk fluorspar procurement and shows that receivables, inventory and supplier balances normalize rather than rolling forward. Fourth, a new same-session price and valuation bridge that puts base value above the entry zone with the required support asymmetry. If all four arrive, the company’s integrated platform could earn a higher quality grade and the verdict should change. If only revenue accelerates while working capital and capex absorb cash, the operating story is improving but the equity still may not compound. This is the advantage of writing down falsifiable gates: you do not need to defend a forecast after the evidence changes. [1][4][6][7]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR’S REFLECTION — do not confuse a lower quote with a better decision
book_callouts.text: What observable filing would change your verdict: the first HFC-32 shipment, two quarters at the margin guide, or cash conversion above PAT? Name the evidence before deciding that a pullback is an opportunity.
